findings.title: Fix the `isAccessTokenId` matcher, which accepts almost any token ID
Null check validates `grantType` twice instead of `rawTokenId`
Grant shortcuts are not validated, so custom grants can produce token IDs that cannot be decoded
Token type is derived from the session context client, not the token's client
Removal of the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor and a new NPE risk in the constructor

response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Title: Fix the `isAccessTokenId` matcher, which accepts almost any token ID

Affected:
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:476-492

Explanation:
The encoded prefix has three 2-character parts: session type, token type, then grant type. The grant shortcut therefore sits at indices 4–6, not 3–5. For `onrtac`, `substring(3, 5)` returns `"ta"`.

The condition is also inverted. It returns `false` when the shortcut *matches* the expected value.

Together, these two bugs mean the matcher passes for almost any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` value. The updated `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` assertions therefore never check the grant type. A wrong grant encoding would go unnoticed. The check also does not verify that the prefix is 6 characters long.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
String[] items = item.split(":");
if (items.length != 2 || items[0].length() != 6) return false;
if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
return isUUID().matches(items[1]);
~~~

## 2) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Null check validates `grantType` twice instead of `rawTokenId`

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73

Explanation:
This line has the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed" but checks `grantType` a second time. A null `rawTokenId` is accepted without error, so `encodeTokenId` can later produce an ID like `onrtac:null`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Grant shortcuts are not validated, so custom grants can produce token IDs that cannot be decoded

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-85
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:106-119
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29-33

Explanation:
The decoder requires the context prefix to be exactly 6 characters, with a 2-character grant shortcut. The `getShortcut()` Javadoc only says "usually like 3-letters", which invites wrong implementations. Nothing enforces the actual rules, so several failures are possible:

- **Wrong length:** a custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` returning a 3-letter shortcut produces token IDs that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects with `IllegalArgumentException`.
- **Colon in the shortcut:** this breaks parsing of the `:` separator.
- **Null shortcut:** this causes an NPE in `ConcurrentHashMap.put` during `postInit`, which blocks server startup.
- **Collision with `"na"`:** this is not clearly reported.

The new method is also abstract with no default. Every existing third-party grant factory will fail to compile or link (`AbstractMethodError`) until it is updated.

Proposed fix:
- In `postInit` and in the lazy-refresh paths, validate that each shortcut is non-null, exactly 2 characters, contains no `:`, and is not `"na"`. Fail with a clear message.
- Correct the Javadoc to say "2 characters".
- Consider a `default` implementation of `getShortcut()` so existing extensions keep working.

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Token type is derived from the session context client, not the token's client

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:54-55
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84-87

Explanation:
`getShouldUseLightweightToken` reads `session.getContext().getClient()`. Before this change it ran only inside mappers. It now runs for every access token created through `initToken`.

That includes paths where the context client may be null, such as admin or internal token generation. I have not verified these paths against code outside the diff. In that case the call throws an NPE and token issuance fails.

In flows like token exchange, the context client can also differ from the client the token is issued to. The encoded lightweight/regular flag would then be wrong.

Proposed fix:
Pass the token's client explicitly and null-check it:
~~~java
ClientModel client = clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient();
boolean lw = Boolean.parseBoolean(client.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED))
        || Boolean.TRUE.equals(session.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED));
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Removal of the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor and a new NPE risk in the constructor

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:87-103

Explanation:
**Copy constructor removed:** the public copy constructor was deleted without deprecation. Any code that clones a `Context` will break, including extensions or other modules not shown here.

**NPE in the main constructor:** it now calls `formParams.getFirst(...)` unconditionally. Any caller passing null `formParams` will get an NPE.

**Stale grant type:** `grantType` is captured once and is not recomputed in `setFormParams`. It can go stale if form params are replaced.

Proposed fix:
- Keep the copy constructor, also copying `grantType`, or deprecate it first.
- Guard against null: `this.grantType = formParams == null ? null : formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`
- Update `grantType` in `setFormParams`.
